notes.title: Sneak Peek at Act 3!
notes.content:
Hello [b]Inkborns[/b]! ✒️ As many of you know, [b]Act 3[/b] is in the works, and today we're ready to give you a little glimpse of what you can expect when you reach it. You’ve fought on the ground and ventured deep underground - now it’s time to rise above it all. ☁️ Get ready to travel to a fractured, mist-covered arena with floating islands, where we're setting the stage for tense encounters. 🌫️

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45298953/5e26cc093d034f4844ed4fd37c636d1adb0d64a6.png[/img]

One of the new enemies you’ll face here is the [b]Apparition[/b]. 
This ghostly foe has a new ability: “[i]Transcendental: Reduces all received damage to 0.[/i]”.
Figuring out how to deal with it will take clever deckbuilding and precise strategy. Can you discover the best way to defeat something that refuses to take a hit? 👻

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45298953/f910175ed168eb21d1533f677de9dfc63018121b.png[/img]

While we wait for the release of Act 3, we’ll be adding an update to the [b]Book of Thoughts[/b], introducing new metaprogression elements to help you prepare for the challenges ahead. And one last thing, we’ve been thinking about adding harder achievements to Inkborn, aimed at the most persistent and determined players. 🏆 For example, an achievement like “[i]Defeat the first Boss using only the starting deck[/i]”.

How would you feel about achievements like this, or do you prefer to keep them a bit more accessible? Let us know in the comments below! 👇

notes.title: 🗡️ Difficulty Levels & Profiles are coming to Inkborn!
notes.content:
Hello everyone! 👋

We’ve just finished preparing the next update for Inkborn, and this one’s special: it features the first two items from our recently published [b]Early Access roadmap[/b]! 🗺️ We’ll keep rolling out more stuff in future updates, step by step, so that every player can enjoy Inkborn in their favorite way. 💪

[h3] 👥 Player Profiles and the Beta Profile [/h3][list]
[*][b]Player Profiles[/b] let you track your progress and manage multiple metaprogression profiles in a single copy of the game.
[*][b]Beta Profile[/b] gives us a way to share some future content with you earlier than planned. In this case: [b]Difficulty Levels[/b].[/list]
Normally, Difficulty Levels would have launched together with Act III, but we’ve seen how much you’re asking for more playtime, so we’ve decided to bring them in sooner. The reason they live in the Beta Profile for now is simple: Difficulty Levels grant extra [b]Soulink[/b], and that speeds up your City progression. If we added them directly into the main profile before Act III, it would curve the intended pacing once Act III drops. 🧭

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45298953/7284ccc2cb52d31564d53e9eee7d0d18fe345b26.png[/img]

👉 So for now, if you want to try out Difficulty Levels, just switch to [b]Beta Profile[/b]. Once Act III is ready, we’ll unlock them for your regular Player Profiles.

[h3]🎚️ Difficulty Levels: choose your challenge[/h3]
After you complete the game for the first time, your next run will give you the option to choose Difficulty modifiers, which crank up the tension and let you tailor how tough each adventure feels. Each completed Level rewards you with [b]1 Soulink[/b], a powerful resource to expand your [b]City[/b] even more. 🏙️[list]
[*][b]Typesetter[/b] up to 3rd level.
[*][b]Shop[/b] up to 3rd level. 
[*][b]Barracks[/b] up to 3rd level.
[*][b]Library[/b] up to 4th level.[/list]
There are [b]10 brand-new Soulinks[/b] up for grabs - and yes, you can attempt a run with all modifiers active to collect them all in one go. But fair warning: this is the kind of run that legends are made of… and also the kind that ends with you questioning all your life choices while yelling. 😀

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45298953/23263f6e992c7addb53b1b8d1008e8c3d9621a39.png[/img]

Here’s the list of modifiers you’ll be able to toggle in this update:[list]
[*]All enemies [b]have 20% more maximum health[/b].
[*]All enemies [b]deal 20% more damage[/b].
[*]All enemies start fights with [b]random buffs[/b].
[*]You have [b]2 Idea slots less[/b].
[*][b]5 additional Chronicle points[/b] for entering map nodes.
[*]Whenever you enter the map node, you lose [b]5 gold[/b].
[*]Camps [b]can't restore health[/b].
[*]Camps [b]can't remove cards[/b].
[*]All prices are increased by [b]25%[/b].
[*]After fights you get [b]1 less card[/b] to choose from.[/list]
Difficulty Levels mark the first step on our [b]Roadmap[/b], and we'll keep adding more ways to play in the patches ahead. Thanks so much for playing and sharing your feedback, it’s been incredibly helpful as we shape Inkborn together. ❤️ We can’t wait to hear about the wild runs you pull off… and how many Soulinks you manage to bring home along the way! 😀

notes.title: What quotes should power the Curse mechanic?
notes.content:
👁️ Hey folks, we’re cooking up something grim for the [b]Curses[/b] in the game, and we’d love your help to make them even more sinister. We’re looking for dark, famous quotes (from books, poems, plays, etc.) that are in the public domain. The kind of lines that feel like a curse whispered into your ear. Think old, eerie lines that send shivers down the spine. A few things to keep in mind:[list]
[*]When sharing citations, please also include the original author’s name and the title of the work.
[*]If the quote isn’t originally in English, please drop the original text too, along with the translator’s name.
[*]Bonus points if it’s something that really feels like it belongs on a cursed relic or whispered by shadows.[/list]
💀 And yes… these quotes aren’t just for flavor. They’ll make your gameplay more challenging. Because why should Curses ever be fair? 😈

Got a favorite grim line that’s stuck with you? [b]Drop it in the comments below![/b] 🕯️ Also, we’ll be giving a shout-out in [b]the Credits[/b] to any community members whose quotes make it into the game. 

P.S.
[b]Difficulty Levels[/b] are almost ready to roll out, keep an eye out for the upcoming updates! 😉

notes.content:

⚔️ Firstly, expect [b]Difficulty Levels[/b]: Whether you want a more relaxed run or a brutal test of your deckbuilding skills, new difficulty options will let you tailor the challenge to your taste. Expect Soulink as reward and bragging rights for braving the harder settings.

🌌 Then, heading straight for [b]the 3rd Act[/b]: A whole new chapter awaits - a fresh environment filled with never-before-seen enemies, treacherous paths, and a climactic finale to push your strategies to the limit.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45298953/ce6af1b8ffd93652a81fcffa30766be177cb9344.png[/img]

[*] [b]Two New Hero Classes:[/b] Each bringing unique mechanics, playstyles, and thematic decks to explore.
[*] [b]New Enemies and Bosses:[/b] More dangerous foes to test your evolving strategies.
[*] [b]More Cards for the 1st Hero Class:[/b] Expand your arsenal with fresh options and synergies.
[*] [b]More Combo combinations:[/b] Unlock new layers of strategy as you experiment with expanded card interactions.
[*] [b]Extended Skill Tree:[/b] More skills to master for the 1st Hero Class, adding depth to progression.
[*] [b]Another wave of Quotes:[/b] New words of wisdom and power to enhance the expedition.
[*] [b]Difficulty Modifiers:[/b] Spice up each run with new modifiers that twist the rules in creative ways.
[/list][h3] 🎮 Planned gameplay features [/h3][list]
[*] [b]Expanded Book of Thoughts:[/b] Integrating a Bestiary filled with lore, enemy details, and story connections.
[*] [b]Bestiary metaprogression:[/b] Unlock bonuses and insights as you encounter and study more creatures.
[*] [b]Chronicle Curses expansion:[/b] Introducing Cursed Quotes and Instant Curses for more variety in run-altering effects.
[*] [b]Story-related Quests:[/b] Undertake story that unveil new chapters of Inkborn’s tapestry, revealing long-lost truths and hidden histories, while granting rare rewards to aid your quest.
[*] [b]Multi-stage events:[/b] Longer, more dynamic encounters with evolving challenges and outcomes.
[*] [b]Quest-like cards:[/b] A fresh card type functioning similarly to story quests, adding tactical objectives mid-run.
[/list][h3] ✨ Quality of Life improvements [/h3][list]
[*] [b]Adjustable animation speed:[/b] Play at your pace, choose slower cinematic animations or fast-forward for rapid action.
[*] [b]Better animation timing:[/b] Smoother, more natural flow to in-game actions.
[*] [b]Fine-tuned visual notifications & pop-ups:[/b] Clearer feedback so you always know what’s happening.
[*] [b]Player Profiles:[/b] Track your progress and play history, manage multiple metaprogression profiles within a single copy of the game. Gain access to upcoming features through the Beta Profile.
[*] [b]Visual progression of buildings:[/b] See your City evolve and grow as you play.
[*] [b]Optimized performance & faster loading:[/b] Reduced waiting times for better, uninterrupted play.
[/list]
This is just the beginning and many surprises still lie ahead. We’ll keep sharing details, sneak peeks, and updates on Steam and in our [url=https://discord.com/invite/UytR7dgwtx]Discord community server[/url]. We’d love to hear what kind of content you’d like to see, your thoughts on what should come first, and any suggestions you have for [b]Inkborn’s[/b] future. This roadmap isn’t set in stone, we’re building it together with you. 👀

The pages of your story are still being written… ink your legacy. ✒️

notes.title: Early Access v0.3.1 Hotfix #1
notes.content:
Hello [b]Inkborns[/b], with the release of [b]version 0.3.1[/b] and the new [i][b]Endless Mode[/b][/i], we discovered a pesky loading screen hiccup. We’ve tracked it down and fixed it, and the hotfix is now live. This issue shouldn’t happen anymore, but if you do run into it, you’ll only lose progress from your current run, not your overall profile.

We’re sorry for any disruption this caused. The version number remains unchanged, but the loading issue affecting some save files has been resolved. Here’s a quick word from our Developer:
[quote]
Hi everyone,

My name is Piotr, though I usually go by my nickname: Pindwin. I lead the technical side of Inkborn’s development, and I thought you might find it interesting to learn what this hotfix is about.

Working on an Early Access title comes with many challenges, and one of the biggest is maintaining backward compatibility while releasing updates, some of which change how your game save is structured. With every update, we need to be extremely careful not to break existing saves. Normally, that’s something you do every few months - not every few days! To stay safe, we built automated systems that compare old saves with new ones, tests that try updating the game save mechanically, and so on. These have worked flawlessly, until now.

And that’s because there’s another challenge in Early Access: rapid change. Last week, when we released Endless Mode, we fell into a trap of our own making, related to how we handle save files. So how did this happen despite all our checks? The short answer: a fixed buffer size.

Inkborn uses a binary save format: each game entity is packed in memory as tightly as possible. Your cards, quotes and ideas, the generated map and shop content - all of that gets an identifier, which we later use to write and recognize the whole card. For example, Greatnib has an identifier of 5, so when we save Greatnib-related info, we don’t write the whole card, we just take 5 as a starting point and apply changes from there. The process is a little more complex, but you get the idea.

This approach keeps even large decks very compact, which makes the game load faster and run smoothly. But—yes, there’s a “but”. This whole process uses a buffer. Think of it like a trolley you use to carry items into storage: you fill the trolley, unload it, and repeat.

In our case, the buffer organizes the save file (the “storage room” in this example). We fill it with different types of items: cards, quotes, enemies, and write them to the file one type at a time. We calculated that even if a player maxed out the entire game, a 4KB buffer would be enough for each item type. So we hardcoded it to use 4,096 bytes of RAM as that trolley.

And then came Endless Mode.

One of the most memory-consuming things we store in a save is statistics. We use them for balance: if a card overperforms or underperforms, we know where to adjust. For ease of analysis, this is one place where we store the names of cards, not just numbers - so the data is easy to read on graphs. One of these stats is every card a player picked during a run. Stored in a memory-heavy way. In a run that can now go endlessly...

Boom. That’s the buffer overflowing-cutting off the card name mid-save. The result? Corrupted saves, which usually show up as combat not ending and the game failing to return to the journey map. If you try to load that save, the game crashes and gets stuck on loading.

The fix? Allow the buffer to grow if needed (from my experience, this happens around Endless 5). Unfortunately, it also means removing some of your old Endless runs.

This probably isn’t the last odd issue caused by unexpected interactions, but we’ll do our best to keep them unnoticeable. ;) I hope sharing their origin stories makes for an interesting read. :)

~Piotr (Pindwin)
[/quote]

notes.title: Endless Mode & Update 0.3.1 is here!
notes.content:
Hey [b]Inkborns[/b]! 👋

As promised, we’re rolling out a [b]new gameplay feature[/b] to help boost replayability while we’re hard at work delivering [b]Difficulty Levels and Act 3[/b]. We get it, those two are highly anticipated at the moment! And while we’re busy shaping what’s next, Endless Mode is here to let you squeeze even more fun out of your carefully built decks, test your strategies, and chase some wild highscores. 🏆

[h3]♾️How Endless Mode works:[/h3]
After successfully defeating the [b]second Act Boss[/b], you’ll now have a choice:
→ end your run and collect all the earned score (EXP points),
→ or enter Endless Mode and continue your journey.

[*] Sharpness: +2 ^ cycle number
[*] HP: Max HP × (1 + 0.25 × cycle number)
[/list]So the first few cycles would look like this:[list]
[*] Cycle 1: +2 Sharpness, Max HP × 1.25
[*] Cycle 2: +4 Sharpness, Max HP × 1.5
[*] Cycle 3: +8 Sharpness, Max HP × 1.75

notes.title: Early Access Release Summary
notes.content:
Hey Inkborns!

First off, a huge thank you for your trust in us and for being so active across all our channels. We’ve been reading everything you’ve shared, from kind words to spot-on feedback and we really appreciate it. 🙏 Your involvement means a lot, and it’s already helped us spot things we can improve.

Now that we’re a few days into [b]Early Access[/b], we want to take a moment to sum things up. In this post, we’ll talk about:
[olist]
[*] What’s been working well.
[*] What didn’t go quite as planned (and what we’re doing about it).
[*] What you can expect from us soon (and a bit later down the line).
[*] A new idea we’re exploring to make the game even more replayable.
[/olist]
[h2]1. What’s been working well.[/h2]

First of all, we’re just really happy to have reached this point. Launching into [b]Early Access[/b] is a huge milestone for us and an important step on the road to version 1.0.

We’re glad to see that the paper-crafted world struck a chord with many of you. Ink is flowing, paper is flying, we’ve already put in an order for more supplies to keep things going. 😉

When it comes to [b]stability[/b], we’re actually feeling pretty good about where things stand. The game isn’t bug-free (yet!), but thanks to your reports, we’ve been able to track down and patch some of the nastier ones pretty fast. First [b]hotfixes are already live[/b], and we’re keeping an eye out for anything else that needs squashing.

We’ve seen a lot of you put in a good number of hours already. 💪 That’s been amazing to watch. Keep hunting down those combos, quoting the literary greats, and slicing through the layers of enemies on your path to victory!

[h2]2. What didn’t go quite as planned (and what we’re doing about it).[/h2]

Not everything went the way we hoped. Some of you mentioned that [b]the game doesn’t offer enough hours of gameplay yet[/b], and yeah, we hear you. We're already working on ways to change that (more on this in a moment).

We also messed up with [b]regional pricing[/b]. In the rush of release, we didn’t catch the issue early enough, and some of you ended up paying more than you should have. What made it worse is that after playing for over 2 hours, Steam wouldn’t let you refund and re-buy the game at the new, lower price. That’s on us, and we want to make it right. If this happened to you, head over to this [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2924580/discussions/0/604163148655838465/]thread[/url][/b], we’ll walk you through the steps to get it sorted. 

[h2]3. What you can expect from us soon (and a bit later down the line).[/h2]

Right now, we’re doing our best to answer your questions and go through all the feedback you’re sending our way. And we’ve got to say, your posts and discussions are incredibly constructive and full of sharp observations. 💪 Please keep them coming!

We owe you a [b]proper roadmap[/b], and yes, it’s on the way! We’ll share it as soon as we can. But we also don’t want to leave you hanging with just a “coming soon” message. Based on what we’re seeing, two things are absolutely key for making your experience more complete:

[list]
[*] [b]Adding Act 3.[/b]
[*] [b]Introducing new systems to boost replayability and raise the challenge.[/b]
[/list]
[b]Act 3[/b] is a major task, especially since we’re sticking to our "no shortcuts" approach when it comes to visuals and quality. But we know how important it is, it’s our top long-term priority. We're currently revisiting our internal schedule to see if we can shift some features around to get [b]Act 3[/b] into your hands sooner. As soon as we’ve got something solid, you’ll be the first to know.

[b]As for replayability and tougher challenges, we’ve decided to speed things up.[/b] Originally, difficulty levels were meant to arrive together with [b]Act 3[/b]. But since it’s clear how important they are to you, we’re moving that up. We’re aiming to introduce difficulty levels by late August or early September.

[b]So, how will they work?[/b]

Once you complete your first full 2-act run, you’ll unlock the [b]difficulty system[/b]. It’s built around modifiers, you pick which ones to enable, each adding a new twist to the challenge. [b]Each modifier comes with a point value[/b], and together they determine your total [b]difficulty score.[/b]

💥And here's the twist: [b]difficulty levels will also tie into your city’s development.[/b] Right now, beating a boss for the first time gives you [b]Soulink[/b]. With difficulty levels, each completed run at a new difficulty will reward additional Soulink, letting you unlock more [b]city upgrades[/b]❗

Since we’re fast-tracking some of these features, [b]we’re also going to add a new Beta Profile option in-game.[/b] That’s where difficulty levels (and possibly other early features) will land first. This way, your main profile stays untouched and keeps progressing at its original pace, while you can jump into the [b]beta profile[/b] to try out what’s next.

[h2]4. A new idea we’re exploring to make the game even more replayable.[/h2]

We came up with an idea that might help make up for the lack of new acts until Act 3 is ready, [b]an Endless Mode[/b]. Endless Mode will let you enjoy a carefully crafted deck and quote combos for much longer. After finishing Act 2, the game would let you jump straight into another loop of the run (with a visit to the city in between) to test yourself against [b]stronger versions of enemies[/b]. 

If that sounds like your kind of fun, we’re already working on getting [b]Endless Mode[/b] ready, maybe as soon as [b]next week.[/b] And if you’re into the idea, we might even add [b]weekly leaderboards[/b] in the future, so you can see who lasts the longest in this endless challenge.

We're curious what you make of the idea. Think it’s worth it? Let us know in the [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2924580/discussions/0/604163148655841247/]thread[/url][/b], your take really helps us decide what to focus on next. We could even tie Endless Mode together with the difficulty levels we mentioned earlier. Be sure to tell us if that would be something you'd find interesting!

[b]In short:[/b]
[olist]
[*] Your feedback really gives us wings!
[*] We know we made some mistakes, and we're fixing them.
[*] Difficulty levels will be added within the next month.
[*] We shared the idea of Endless Mode, if you like it, we plan to launch it next week, but we need your feedback first.
[*] While you’re enjoying the new difficulty levels and (hopefully!) Endless Mode, we’ll be working on the Roadmap and Act 3.
[/olist]
[b]Thank you for being with us, it truly means a lot![/b]

Here’s a little sneak peek of what’s coming 😉

notes.title: 🛠️ Beta Update 0.2.1 is Live!
notes.content:
Bug fixes, balance tweaks, quality-of-life improvements - and yes, the Kind Faerie has her wings again. 🧚

Thanks for playing and testing [b]Inkborn[/b]! This patch focuses on improving stability, fixing soft locks, and making the overall gameplay experience smoother and more readable.

🔽 Full changelog below:
[Feature] The Kind Faerie has wings again!
[Feature] Added background music to the Main Menu.
[QoL] Dialogue scroll speed has been increased.
[QoL] It's now easier to visually distinguish Common vs. Rare Ideas.
[QoL] Adjusted the positioning of HUD tooltips for better visibility.
[Fix] Random encounters now properly randomize as intended.
[Fix] Added missing localization to Evergrowing Roots’ attacks.
[Fix] Loading a save will now correctly restore the previous combat state.
[Fix] The summary screen now displays the defeated boss, if applicable.
[Fix] Added a missing icon for the illumination status.
[Fix] Rare cards now truly live up to their name and have a lower drop rate.
[Fix] Dragon’s intent has been moved lower on the screen.
[Fix] The Draw Pile button is now disabled outside of combat.
[Fix] Enemies that summon reinforcements should no longer cause battle positioning issues.
[Fix] Fixed a soft lock in the “Cartographer” event.
[Fix] Fixed a soft lock caused by Mary Shelley’s torso quote.
[Fix] The Destiny-Pointing Signpost now correctly doubles the reward only once.
[Fix] Curse cards can no longer be upgraded.
[Fix] Shop cards now show tooltips correctly and no longer appear as upgraded.
[Fix] The Mantis enemy now only consumes other Mantises (no more snack time across species).

We're grateful for all the feedback so far, it’s helping us shape [b]Inkborn [/b]into something truly special. Keep those reports coming, and we’ll see you in the next run! 🌀

notes.title: Your feedback will come to life in the Early Access version of Inkborn!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45298953/883c069489f4a57bfa52d6234dc0d18440ab2a8e.jpg[/img]

Hello, roguelike deckbuilders enthusiasts!

[b]At the very beginning of this announcement, we would like to sincerely thank once more all of you who have checked out the Inkborn Combat Demo so far and shared your feedback on the gameplay experience with us. We are very grateful to you for this action, as your feedback will help us make our game that much better![/b]

We took a very careful look at the feedback you received, not only via social media channels or the Inkborn Discord server but also the one you sent to us directly from the demo version itself.

You have shared with us a lot of hints on the mechanics and features implemented in Inkborn. There are still a few things we need to improve, but with your support, we will succeed! 💪🏼

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45298953/0a3c58b03d245f3fc1dfc25ffa347da334eafca8.png[/img]

You’ve asked us about various aspects of the game, like the volume of the music in the demo, the visibility of Ideas, the ability to skip cards when adding them to the deck, and similarities to Slay the Spire. [b]Our dev team has reviewed all these points: some fixes have already been implemented, while others are awaiting integration in the Early Access version. But that’s not all![/b]

Some of you reached out to us directly from the demo’s menu with feedback about the dodge mechanism, suggestions for improvements (such as “[i]Highlight or bold text in the Book of Thoughts[/i]” or “[i]When choosing a quote, it would be nice if you could hover over the bonus as well to pick it, not just the slots[/i]”), and clear, detailed bug reports. We truly appreciate it! 

And, of course, you didn’t stop there! ❤️

[b]While we are thankful for your feedback and suggestions, we want to clarify that we won't update the game's demo version. Instead, we're focusing on refining the Early Access to ensure the best possible experience for everyone.[/b] However, we would like to respond to the messages we received, so here's a structured response for better clarity:

[list]
[*] [b]We will introduce additional healing options[/b]; its absence is a characteristic of the demo.
[*] [b]We are considering various accessibility and quality-of-life (QoL) improvements[/b] in further development.
[*] [b]We are working on improving the UI for quotes[/b].
[*] We recognize that animations need fine-tuning, so [b]we plan to synchronize attack animations with sound effects[/b].
[*] [b]We’ll review the balance of Inkbreath’s move[/b].
[*] [b]We monitor and optimize combo balance and overall game balance[/b].
[*] [b]We make game elements more self-evident[/b] (e.g., damage numbers and descriptions).
[*] [b]We are evaluating the design of certain characters[/b], and some may undergo significant changes.
[/list]
Furthermore, we’d like to reveal, especially for everyone who gave us feedback, some additional exciting plans:

[list]
[*] [b]We plan to introduce new combos and cards in the future[/b].
[*] [b]We will add a lot more sound effects[/b].
[*] In the Early Access version, beyond the combat mechanics you’ve already experienced, [b]you can expect city upgrades, a skill tree, exploration mechanics, and a chronicle system[/b].
[*] [b]We will take a closer look at the text field[/b].
[/list]
In our humble opinion, it’s worth the wait ;)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45298953/e1eb977e964955cef6ff2cf393bdde6427af1bb9.png[/img]

And that would be it! [b]We catalog and collect your feedback in one place, and our dev team constantly improves the game and works on its improvements to the Early Access version.[/b] Of course, remember to add Inkborn to your wishlist, follow our social media channels, and leave your thoughts. Your feedback is a valuable motivation for us to continue working on Inkborn!
